subject: Request: evidence of no exfiltration after token rotation ripple
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@fintech-escrow.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: sec-team@fintech-escrow.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Request: evidence of no exfiltration after token rotation ripple

Hi Grace,

Following yesterday's transient token rotation event your team mentioned on the status page, our security team is asking for a concise confirmation that there was no data exfiltration from our tenant (FinTech Escrow) or any wider leakage affecting our accounts.

Specifically, can you provide:
- Confirmation whether any outbound connections or unusual egress were observed tied to our tenant IDs between 2027-03-21T02:00Z and 2027-03-21T06:00Z.
- Results of any log integrity checks or hash verifications you ran (sample hashes are fine).
- Any artifacts / redacted logs we can use for our audit team (PDF or plain text).

We need something we can attach to our internal post-incident record today — a short statement and any supporting artifacts are sufficient. Please let me know timeline; we can escalate on our side if you need fast turnaround.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Security Engineer, FinTech Escrow
olivia@fintech-escrow.com

---
Note: requested timeframe is narrow — if you need a slightly different window for correlation we can accept that as long as the statement covers the scope of potential exposure.
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@fintech-escrow.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence of no exfiltration after token rotation ripple

Hi Olivia — thanks for the note and for the clear list of deliverables. Hannah and Marcus are looped in; Marcus will own the technical scan and I'll coordinate delivery and the audit artifact.

Planned next steps:
1) Marcus will run a focused integrity scan across the access logs and network egress telemetry for your tenant IDs for the window you specified (and plus/minus 30 minutes for safety).
2) We'll compute SHA-256 hashes of the sampled log files and provide a short PDF with the methodology and results.
3) We'll provide a redacted sample of the raw log lines used for the hash (PII/email redacted).

Timeline: we expect an initial statement + artifacts within 24 hours. If anything looks anomalous we'll escalate immediately and share timelines.

Permission: please confirm we have permission to pull the relevant log files / telemetry from your org context for this scan. We will not share live raw logs beyond the redacted samples.

If you confirm, Marcus will start and I will follow up with the report.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@fintech-escrow.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Confirmation and artifacts — FinTech Escrow integrity scan (no exfiltration found)

Hi Olivia — attaching our artifacts and short confirmation for your audit record. Summary first, details below.

Summary conclusion: No evidence of data exfiltration or unauthorized outbound transfers tied to FinTech Escrow tenant IDs during the reviewed window (2027-03-21T01:30:00Z through 2027-03-21T06:30:00Z).

What we checked:
- Access and control-plane logs (all token operations) for your tenant IDs; compared pre/post-rotation sequences.
- Egress telemetry across outbound network flows originating from inference hosts correlated to your tenant IDs.
- Integrity verification: computed SHA-256 on sampled log files at source; compared to stored golden hashes in our immutable log store.
- Process and host-level checks for abnormal fork/exec patterns and sudden spool-to-disk activity during the window.
- Destination IP / TLS SNI analysis for outbound connections — flagged and reviewed any non-standard destinations.

Artifacts included (attached):
- integrity_scan_report_20270322.pdf — condensed methodology and findings (2 pages).
- sha256_sample_hashes.txt — list of filenames and SHA-256 digests for the sampled files (hashes computed on our side; you can reproduce with the attached KQL queries).
- redacted_kql_queries.txt — KQL used to extract samples (columns with PII redacted).

Key observations and assurance notes:
- Sampled file hashes matched the immutable store's recorded hashes. No alteration detected for sampled segments (samples taken across the time window and across three different host pools).
- Egress analysis: all outbound flows from the correlated containers/auth contexts terminated in known cloud provider ranges or internal telemetry sinks. No connections to previously unseen hosts.
- Audit trails: user tokens used during rotation were short-lived and matched rotation logs. No replay attempts or token misuse identified in our control-plane logs.
- Scope limitation: hashes and samples are partial by design (we provide representative samples and methodology so your auditors can reproduce). If you require a full-file-level audit we can discuss next steps and timeline.

Next steps / recommended language for your record (copyable):
"Redwood Inference scanned access logs and egress telemetry for FinTech Escrow for the interval 2027-03-21T01:30:00Z — 2027-03-21T06:30:00Z. We found no evidence of unauthorized data exfiltration or data leakage affecting FinTech Escrow during that interval. A representative sample of log files was hashed and verified against Redwood's immutable log store; sample hashes are provided in sha256_sample_hashes.txt."

If you want us to: 1) run a wider time-range scan, 2) provide additional hash samples, or 3) generate a signed statement on company letterhead, please indicate and we'll prioritize.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: integrity_scan_report_20270322.pdf (PDF), sha256_sample_hashes.txt (text), redacted_kql_queries.txt (text)
